sources.title: QMA=PP implies that PP contains PH
sources.locator: Theorem1 pp.5–6; Theorem2 pp.7–8; Corollaries1–2 p.8
sources.quote: If QMA = PP then QMA = PP ⊇ PH.
sources.notes: Corollary2 assumes coCeqP=PP. A stronger CeqP⊆QMA premise is not a stated theorem and is held for independent derivation review.

sources.title: Quantum Arthur–Merlin Games
sources.locator: Definition of QMA; Theorem3.3 amplification, Theorem3.4 and Remark3.5, pp.13–14
sources.notes: Also QMA⊆A0PP. Bounded-error total languages are obtained by requiring the verifier gap on every input.

sources.title: Complexity Limitations on Quantum Computation
sources.locator: Definition2.1 and following paragraph, p.3; Theorem3.1, Theorem3.3, Corollaries3.4–3.5, pp.5–7
sources.quote: BQP machines can simulate deterministic Turing machines and other BQP machines as subroutines
sources.notes: BQP⊆AWPP and AWPP is PP-low. The subroutine paragraph cites Bernstein–Vazirani1997. Classical adaptive-query simulation needs only amplification and polynomial composition.

sources.title: The Size of SPP

sources.notes: The subsequent PH⊆SPP equivalence explicitly adds the hypothesis that NP has nonzero p-measure. Do not discard that premise.

semantics_review.finding: No concrete semantic mismatch confirmed in assigned definitions. This is source inspection, not a completed Lean equivalence proof.
checks: Nondeterministic transition lists retain branch multiplicity; allBranchesHaltWithin excludes truncating nonhalting branches; early accepting leaves count once.
Existential runtime functions must be polynomially bounded and bound a single finite-control machine on every input; they do not add advice.
UP and FewP restrict accepting count globally; coUP is language complement. GapP is a difference of two actual SharpP functions.
CeqP tests zero, PP tests strictly positive integer gap, parityP tests odd accepting count. Threshold conventions are convertible.
SPP tests exact characteristic values. AWPP universally quantifies requested explicit error polynomial and has nonnegative gap bounded by a power-of-two polynomial normalizer on every input.

LWPP and WPP use genuine uniform polynomial-time integer transducers. A nonzero signed normalizer is equivalent to a positive one by multiplying gap and normalizer by the normalizer. Unary input to LWPP prevents covert dependence on input contents.
Quantum gates are explicit H,T,X,CNOT with distinct control/target. Circuit serialization and finite-control generator prohibit an arbitrary uncomputable circuit family.

QMA quantifies normalized pure quantum witnesses; mixed states cannot improve a linear acceptance functional beyond pure states. QCMA quantifies basis witnesses. BQP uses the unique zero-qubit basis state.
Quantum input, witness and zero ancilla registers are disjoint; fixed explicit polynomial witness/ancilla lengths allow padding. Constant completeness and soundness bounds apply to every input.
semantics_review.minor_documentation_observation: Counting.lean introductory comment still says LWPP/WPP omitted, although they are now concretely defined in Transducers.lean. This does not change a class.

padding_review.derivation: Choose exact polynomial padding length p(n)≥n+1, e.g. (n+2)^k. The padded exponential-time language is in E/NE. Deterministic padding preserves accepting multiplicity, FP normalizers and polynomial time. LWPP uses h(0^{p(n)}); AWPP chooses padded error dominating original requested error. Quantum generators compose with p(n), hardwire suffix and pad witnesses without changing acceptance.
padding_review.small_input_caveat: Do not use n^k−n−1 padding blindly at n=0 or1; fix finitely many lengths or use (n+2)^k.
